Issued at 219 PM CDT Sun Aug 9 2026

West/northwest flow aloft continues over the region on the 
downstream side of a low amplitude ridge over the western CONUS and 
southwest of the ongoing large low/trough over the Hudson Bay. This 
evening through the overnight hours, another weak embedded shortwave 
(35-50kts) will move in out of MT/WY and track east/southeast across 
the Dakotas/MN through Monday morning. At the surface the CWA is 
sandwiched between a high to our north with an elongated northwest 
to southeast frontal boundary along the lee of the Rockies (and 
several weak lows along it) connecting to a wesFor 
example HRRR/RAP do not show any development of storms, like at 
all, with NAMNest keeping any convection over north central SD 
while FV3 keeps convection over south central SD and south of 
the CWA with more of a easterly track.t to east frontal 
boundary, and its low, over the Central Plains. This leaves the 
Northern Plains on the northern side of this system with east to 
northeast winds at the surface to 850mb. WAA will filter in 
overnight as these winds will shift south/southeasterly across the 
CWA through Monday morning with surface dewpoints in the upper 50s 
and 60s across the CWA. 

Regarding potential convection tonight, the latest runs of the 12Z 
models have backed off quite a bit on the development and evolution 
of thunderstorms resulting in very low confidence in potential 
outcome. Due to this, stuck with NBM for much of the near short term 
in terms of pops. As of now, HREF mean indicates the development of 
storms moving in over north central SD (around ~3-5Z), which is 
about the same time we have weak shortwave pulses over this area. If 
these cells do in fact form initially, the environment is favorable 
for supercells as MuCape/MLCape is forecast between 1000-2500j/kg 
(Rap higher with values 2500-3500 j/kg over potions of central SD) 
with bulk shear between 40-50kts (again RAP higher at 50-60kts) and 
steep mid level lapse rates between 7-8C/km into the cooler air 
aloft. Given the elevated nature and parameters mentioned, large 
hail will be the main threat early on, especially with any 
development of elevated supercells or splitting supercells per 
elongated hodographs above the surface. Within the Slight Risk over 
central SD, the probability of severe hail is 15-29%, with a cig 1 
hatch (2"+ in diameter potential), over north central SD, mainly 
locations along and west of the Mo River. If additional convection 
develops through the night, this could result in mergers and 
clusters that could grow upscale as the system tracks east or
southeast. If this occurs, then the main threat would become 
more of a damaging wind gust of 60-70 mph or potentially higher 
gusts above 75 mph if a RIJ/bow forms. SPC highlights this 
threat as well over central SD giving the cig 1 hatched (74mph+ 
wind threat) per SPC along and south of a line from Mobridge to 
Redfield. However, the caveat to all of this is that everything 
needs to come together and line up timing wise an there seems to
be quite a bit of disagreement between the CAMs as mentioned on
timing, storm mode, and track with the possibility of nothing 
developing.

Not too much change in the pattern aloft for Monday and Tuesday with 
the region in overall zonal to northwest flow. Weak embedded 
shortwave/pulses will track east/southeast over the area Monday 
evening into Tuesday morning and again Tuesday evening into 
Wednesday morning in tandem with CAPE of 1500+j/kg and wind
shear 30+kts along with ongoing low level moisture. Higher 
amounts of CAPE and dewpoints potentially in the lower 70s look 
possible Tuesday afternoon/evening. The pattern of discrete 
cells potentially growing upscale looks to continue, therefore 
large hail and wind gusts of 60-70+ mph will be the main 
threats. A Marginal Risk for severe weather is outlooked over 
the entire CWA Monday and Tuesday. Otherwise, this ongoing 
pattern results in chances of precip through the end of the 
week. This flow will lead to ongoing smoke aloft with not much 
in the way of near surface smoke. With this setup, temps will be
near normal (ranging in the 80s) with stronger CAA developing 
for the end of the week (strengthening trough out east) with 
highs a good 5-10 degrees below average and forecast highs in 
the 70s!
